text:
alex: Heads-up — product is planning a short flash promo on Dec 2 for APAC (6h window). We should run a dry-run next week to validate capacity and fallbacks.

maria: +1. Proposed dry-run: simulate 2x baseline QPS with 30s median latency SLO. Can we also exercise region failover? :earth_asia:

tariq: We can do a synthetic workload against staging clusters. Need to confirm GPU hour budget for the day — last promo burned more than forecast.

alex: Budget target for promo: keep additional GPU hours under 1.2k for the 6h window, otherwise devs have asked for autoscale burst up to 1.8k if SLAs degrade.

sam: Who's owning the routing policy for APAC? If Singapore saturates we should spill to Osaka, not to US-west.

maria: I'll own routing. Current policy prioritizes same-region, then nearest region. We'll change to prefer APAC secondaries first.

infra-bot: [alert] cluster-stg-sg: GPU util spike 85% (5m avg). Automated scaling triggered +2 nodes.

emily: For the dry run, can we pre-warm KV cache for the most common prefixes? That saved ~18% tokens on last test.

tariq: Yes — we can load top 200 prompt prefixes. I'll produce a small script.

alex: Can someone post the quick command to query remaining reserved capacity so PMs know the constraint?

maria: Use the infra API:

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://infra-api.redwood.local/v1/capacity/reserved?region=apac"
```

Response has fields: reserved_gpus, used_gpus, pending_bursts.

sam: Also add a quick check to ensure network egress quotas in SG aren't the blocker. Ran into a cap last year.

emily: I'll add a small egress check:

```
kubectl -n infra get quota net-egress-sg -o yaml
```
If usage > 80% we flag and request bump.

tariq: Here's the load generator plan (staging): 3 lanes: cold-starts (30% requests), hot-KV (50%), batched long tails (20%). Run for 90m ramp, 3h steady, 30m cool-down.

alex: Good. What about model fallbacks? If large Llama-2 quantized variant fails, we want an automatic fallback to q4f medium. Maria, can you add a canary with 5% split to the fallback path during the dry-run?

maria: Yep — adding canary rule to routing config. Example snippet:

```
route_rules:
  - match: region==apac
    fallback_order: [apac-quantized, apac-q4f-med, global-q4f-med]
    canary: {percent: 5, duration: "30m"}
```

alex: Nice. Cost control: if projected GPU hours exceed 1.2k, infra should throttle non-production traffic first. Is that automated?

tariq: We have a budget watch job. It emits slack alerts at 65%, 85%, and 100% of budget. At 85% it will start rejecting low-priority (tag=dev) routes. We need to ensure test traffic is tagged correctly.

emily: I'll add tagging rules to the load generator: `--tag dev-dryrun`.

infra-bot: [notice] budget-watch: APAC promo budget at 40% (ETA: +8h at current burn).

sam: Network flakiness note: last time we saw increased SYN retries from one SG AZ. Recommend we run the dry-run across two AZs and include 5% of traffic forced into AZ-B to surface issues.

maria: Good catch. Will configure AZ affinity: 95% AZ-A, 5% AZ-B for the test.

alex: Timeline: dry-run next Tue 03:00 UTC (convenient for APAC). 30m pre-check, 4h test (shorter than prod), 30m cool down. Who can be on-call for first response?

sam: I can. 03:00-06:00 UTC.

tariq: I'll be there for runtime metrics and to push cache preload.

emily: I'll monitor egress quota and cost. Maria will watch routing.

alex: Perfect. Action items summary:
- maria: update routing fallback + canary and AZ affinity
- tariq: load gen script + prefix preload + tagging
- emily: egress and budget watch validation
- sam: on-call and escalation lead
- infra-bot: post run summary into this thread when done

maria: Filing a short runbook PR now: https://git.redwood/infra/runbooks/promo-dryrun (draft)

sam: One more ask — can we capture a short-turn metric: p99 tail-latency by tenant tier (free/pro/enterprise)? Want to ensure promo doesn't blow up free-tier SLA unexpectedly.

tariq: We'll emit tenant-tier label in traces and extract p99.

infra-bot: [info] scheduled-job: dryrun-loadgen will run at 1769923200 (Tue 03:00 UTC).

alex: Great, thanks all. If anything changes ping @channel.

maria: Will follow up with runbook PR link once merged. :rocket:
